site.title: Northgate Credit Union | Banking for members across the upper Midwest
site.description: A member-owned credit union with 22 branches in Minnesota, Wisconsin and Iowa. Personal banking, mortgages and small business lending.
site.markdown:
# Banking that stays in your town

Northgate is owned by its members and run from 22 branches across Minnesota, Wisconsin and Iowa.

## Small business lending

Northgate opened a small business lending team in 2023. It writes loans for owner-operated businesses in every county we serve, and the decision is made by a lender who has visited the business.

## Mortgages and personal banking

Fixed and adjustable mortgages, home equity lines, auto loans and everyday accounts.

## Leadership

Marcus Odhiambo joined Northgate as chief lending officer in August, after twelve years in commercial lending at a regional bank.

## Branches

Find a branch near you. Every branch has a lender on site.

writing.markdown:
# Northgate news

## A note from our new chief lending officer

By Marcus Odhiambo

I joined Northgate in August after twelve years in commercial lending at a regional bank. My first job is to listen. I am visiting all 22 branches before the end of the year and sitting with the lending teams, because the people who meet members every day know where the book should grow and where it should not.

## Fall member meeting

The annual member meeting is on the second Tuesday of November at the main branch.

data.invite_line: You joined Northgate as chief lending officer in August and set out to visit all 22 branches before the end of the year. Our readers would like to know what you heard on the way, and what it changed in the lending book.
data.episode_title: Listening to 22 branches before changing the lending book
data.angle: The piece would follow the branch visits: what the lending teams told you, where small business lending has grown fastest since the program opened in 2023, and which parts of a regional bank's commercial lending playbook carry over to a credit union and which do not. We would end on the lending book itself: how you decide what to grow next, and how you explain that to a board. No product talk from our side and no company history. Your answers run as written, edited only for length.
